subject: Order Form: cashflow routing, tax responsibilities & redline coordination
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form: initial redlines from FinTools (pricing / tax / invoicing)

Team — attaching FinTools' latest redlines to the Order Form (FinTools_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx). High level items they changed that need negotiation:

- Net terms: they pushed Net60 on procurement; original orderform says Net30/Net45 depending on tier.
- Invoice routing: they want all invoices to go to their AP remit (FinTools US entity) regardless of service region — we need to confirm whether this is acceptable for VAT/GST handling.
- Tax responsibility: they added a clause that Redwood will bear withholding tax and any local tax liabilities in certain jurisdictions and asked for a gross-up.
- Backcharge / audit: they added a broad backcharge clause that could allow them to recover perceived downtime costs without prior notice.
- Minimum commit phasing: they want the minimum commit to be pro-rated across three tranches and allow credits for unused tokens after 6 months.

As next steps I need:
1) Marissa — commercial position on Net60 vs Net45 (we can compromise with early-pay discount or milestone deposit). Also comment on whether we can accept pro-rated commit + crediting mechanism — any impact to recognition / cashflow?
2) Karthik — quick read of the tax and backcharge language (attached pages highlighted). Can we propose language that limits backcharges to documented third-party costs and requires notice + cure period? For tax, what's acceptable compromise on withholding/gross-up and evidence we should request?

Goal: get a redline back to FinTools legal by EOD Friday (Dec 10) so procurement can keep their timeline.

Attachments: FinTools_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx (track-changes)

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form: initial redlines from FinTools (pricing / tax / invoicing)

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 9:15 AM Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — attaching FinTools' latest redlines to the Order Form...

Thanks for the heads up, Rohan. Quick commercial reactions below — I kept things pragmatic because FinTools is on a fast timeline.

Net terms:
- Prefer to avoid Net60. If they insist, propose Net45 with an early-pay discount of 1% if paid within 15 days. That preserves cashflow and gives procurement what they want tactically.

Invoice routing & currency:
- We cannot have all EU/ROW invoices routed to a US entity without tax impact. Propose language: invoices for EU services to EU entity (or billed with VAT as required) and US services to the US remit. We can include an AP-oriented clause: "Customer shall ensure invoices are routed to the appropriate legal entity for VAT/GST purposes; Redwood will provide invoice metadata upon request."

Taxes & withholding:
- We should not accept a full gross-up. Instead: customer responsible for local taxes/withholding; Redwood will provide tax residency evidence and invoices adjusted for VAT where applicable. If withholding applies, Customer must provide proof (withholding tax receipts) and Redwood will cooperate on gross-up only where statutorily required.

Minimum commit phasing & credits:
- OK with pro-rated commit across three tranches provided: 1) each tranche invoiced in advance for the quarter; 2) unused credits expire after 6 months (or convert to overage discounts). Need finance to confirm revenue recognition but this structure is workable.

Backcharges / audit:
- Strongly recommend limiting backcharges to "direct third-party costs" with a 30-day notice and cure period. Remove vague loss language that allows retrospective service credits without evidence.

Attached a short tax residency sheet I compiled for likely EU concerns: FinTools_TaxResidency_Sheet.xlsx.

If Karthik can draft suggested redlines for tax/backcharge clauses, I can take the commercial edits and produce a consolidated redline to return to FinTools legal.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: FinTools_TaxResidency_Sheet.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTools Legal <legal@fintools.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form: initial redlines from FinTools (pricing / tax / invoicing)

Rohan / Marissa — thanks for the context and the attachments. I reviewed the customer's redline and provide proposed language and risk notes below. I copied FinTools Legal so they see our position early.

1) Tax / Withholding / Gross-up (proposed compromise)
Proposed clause to offer the customer: "Customer will be responsible for all taxes, duties, and withholdings imposed by its jurisdiction in connection with amounts payable under this Agreement; except that Redwood will be responsible for taxes based on Redwood's net income. If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold taxes from amounts payable to Redwood, Customer shall (a) withhold the minimum required by law, (b) provide Redwood with official documentation of the withholding within 30 days, and (c) where statutorily required and only to the extent permitted by law, cooperate in seeking tax credits or refunds. Redwood and Customer will use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate double taxation."

- Rationale: avoids broad gross-up obligation while committing to cooperation and documentation. We should also attach evidence (certificate of tax residency) at signing.

2) Backcharge / Service Credits (proposed language)
- Replace their broad clause with: "Customer may request reimbursement for direct, documented third-party costs reasonably incurred as a result of a material breach by Redwood, provided Customer provides written notice describing the alleged breach and supporting documentation, and allows Redwood a 30-day cure period. Any reimbursement is limited to documented third-party costs reasonably incurred and shall exclude indirect, incidental, or consequential damages."

- Rationale: limits exposure and includes cure period. Keeps commercial leverage for remedies but prevents open-ended chargebacks.

3) Invoice Routing / Currency
- We cannot accept a clause that requires Redwood to re-route invoices across legal entities at the customer's whim. Proposed compromise: invoices will be issued by the Redwood legal entity performing the service; Customer shall instruct its AP to remit to the bank account specified on the invoice. If Customer requests alternate invoicing entity for tax reasons, we will consider with written notice and provide documentation (W-8/W-9 or local equivalents) and adjusted orderform.

4) Minimum Commit / Credits
- Acceptable to have tranches, but each tranche should be invoiced in advance and be non-refundable; unused credits may be credited once and expire after 6 months. If they want a separate repayment/credit mechanism, require higher minimum or prepayment.

5) Doc references & MSA
- I attached the current MSA (signed-msa-draft.pdf) with inline comments on sections relating to audit, confidentiality and indemnities. Biggest legal ask: remove blanket indemnity tied to taxes — handle on a jurisdictional basis.

Next steps:
- Marissa, can you consolidate commercial edits and produce a single clean redline we can send to FinTools Legal?
- Rohan, recommend scheduling a 30-min calibration call with FinTools procurement + legal early next week (Dec 7/8) to walk key asks — let me know availability.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: signed-msa-draft.pdf
From: Angela Park <apark@fintools.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form: initial redlines from FinTools (pricing / tax / invoicing)

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turn. Samir (Procurement) pushed back on Net45; he wants to keep Net60 as AP policy, but we can discuss an early-pay discount. We also need the MSA executed before they will approve any pre-payment schedule.

On taxes: FinTools can provide tax residency certificates and the requested withholding receipts where applicable. We are not comfortable accepting liability for gross-ups in territories where statutory withholding applies; our view is that local withholding is the customer's obligation, but we will be flexible on documentation and cooperation.

On backcharges: FinTools is willing to accept a 30-day notice/cure period but requests that certain service-impacting incidents allow for immediate credits in the event of prolonged outages (we can capture definition / SLAs in the Order Form).

Next steps:
1) Please send consolidated redline including the backcharge wording and tax compromise you outlined.
2) Can Redwood provide a single-page payment schedule showing tranche amounts and invoice dates for the three tranches? Procurement would like that to present to their CFO.
3) We will review the MSA comments and aim to return a counter-redline by Dec 15.

DocuSign link for MSA review: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/AA1234567

Regards,
Angela Park
